summary: Audit export lag (30–60 min) to Datadog Logs during peak hours (backlog growth + suspected intake throttling)
description:
Customer report (via Support): Audit events exported to Datadog Logs are arriving 30–60 minutes late during their peak traffic window (approx. 16:30–19:00 UTC). Outside peak, export latency returns to <5 minutes.

Impact:
- Security team cannot rely on near-real-time alerting/correlation (e.g., admin role changes, API key rotations).
- Compliance monitoring workflows impacted for the duration of lag.

Customer details:
- Customer: Echelon Health
- Destination: Datadog Logs intake (US)
- SIEM-ready audit export beta enabled for workspace(s): EH-PROD, EH-SEC (per Console)

Observed symptoms (Redwood side):
- audit-export delivery backlog steadily increases during peak; drains overnight.
- Connector errors correlate with intake 429/5xx responses.

Dashboards / graphs (internal):
- Audit Export Overview (us-east): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/audit-export/overview?var=region=us-east
  - delivery_latency_p95 spikes from ~2m to 45–70m during peak
  - backlog_depth increases from ~0–5k to ~180k events
- Datadog connector errors: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/audit-export/connectors?var=sink=datadog&var=region=us-east
  - sustained 429 rate-limited responses, intermittent 502/503

Initial hypothesis:
- Datadog intake throttling (429) combined with conservative worker concurrency/backoff causes backlog growth.
- Potential amplification from customer’s event volume increase + filter changes (more event types included).

Requested from customer:
- Confirm Datadog intake endpoint + any org-level rate limits.
- Confirm whether additional tags/attributes were recently added (larger payload size).

Next actions (internal):
1) Validate error classification and retry behavior (ensure we’re not treating 429 as hard failure).
2) Apply temporary mitigation: cap batch size, increase concurrency within safe bounds, and enable circuit-breaker behavior to avoid retry storms.
3) If needed, advise customer to add Datadog log pipeline filters on their side or tighten export filters to reduce volume until tuning is complete.

Slack references:
- #support thread: https://slack.redwood.internal/archives/C-support/p1739186632
- #incidents thread: https://slack.redwood.internal/archives/C-incidents/p1739201120

Notes:
- This ticket is about lag (backlog), not missing events. Delivery is at-least-once; duplicates are possible under retry (see SUP-23145).

resolution:
Resolved via service-side tuning to reduce backlog amplification under Datadog throttling:
- Reduced Datadog connector batch size to lower payload size and improve acceptance rate.
- Increased per-destination concurrency within a safe global cap.
- Updated retry logic to honor Retry-After for 429 with jittered exponential backoff; improved error classification to avoid prolonged retry chains.

Outcome:
- Peak-window backlog growth reduced significantly; p95 delivery latency improved from ~45–70 mins to ~15–22 mins in us-east.

Customer communication:
- Confirmed at-least-once delivery semantics and that lag was due to destination throttling + backlog.
- Provided temporary workaround: tighten export filters during peak if lower latency is required.

Follow-ups (not blockers for closing this SUP ticket):
- Add alerting on sustained 429 + backlog slope and document Datadog intake/rate-limit guidance for beta customers.
